root_semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: For all integers m >= 2 and all integers g >= 0, the counting function N(m,g) is monotonically nondecreasing in g with step size 1: N(m,g) <= N(m,g+1).

payload.theorem_nl: For every integer m >= 2 and every integer g >= 0, the number N(m, g) of numerical semigroups with multiplicity m and genus g satisfies N(m, g) <= N(m, g + 1).

assembly_plan.proof_skeleton_nl: Split into two genus ranges. In the low-genus range g < m-1, use the multiplicity obstruction to show A_{m,g} is empty, hence N(m,g)=0 and the inequality is immediate. In the range g >= m-1, define a canonical child map by deleting the least effective generator of each numerical semigroup S in A_{m,g}. The existence of an effective generator makes this map well-defined, and deleting such a generator preserves multiplicity while increasing genus by exactly one. Parent recovery from the child's Frobenius number yields injectivity of this map. Finally, an injection A_{m,g} -> A_{m,g+1} implies N(m,g) <= N(m,g+1). Combining the two ranges proves the theorem for all g >= 0.

steps.derives: For every integer m >= 2 and every integer g with 0 <= g < m-1, one has N(m,g)=0.
steps.trivial_justification: This is exactly the concluding clause of L1.

steps.derives: For every integer m >= 2 and every integer g >= m-1, the rule S ↦ C(S), where C(S)=S\{e(S)} and e(S) is the least effective generator of S, maps A_{m,g} into A_{m,g+1}.
steps.trivial_justification: From L6, whenever S is a numerical semigroup with multiplicity m and genus at least m-1, C(S) is well-defined, has multiplicity m, and satisfies g(C(S))=g(S)+1. Specializing to S in A_{m,g} gives C(S) in A_{m,g+1}.

steps.derives: For every integer m >= 2 and every integer g >= m-1, the canonical map C : A_{m,g} -> A_{m,g+1} is injective.
steps.trivial_justification: This is precisely the assertion of L7.

steps.derives: For every integer m >= 2 and every integer g >= m-1, one has N(m,g) <= N(m,g+1).
steps.trivial_justification: A3 provides an injective function A_{m,g} -> A_{m,g+1}; L8 converts that injection into the cardinality inequality.

steps.derives: If m >= 2 and g >= 0 satisfy g < m-1, then N(m,g) <= N(m,g+1).
steps.trivial_justification: By A1, N(m,g)=0. Since N(m,g+1) is a cardinality, it is a nonnegative integer. Therefore 0 <= N(m,g+1), so N(m,g) <= N(m,g+1).

steps.derives: For every integer m >= 2 and every integer g >= 0, the number N(m, g) of numerical semigroups with multiplicity m and genus g satisfies N(m, g) <= N(m, g + 1).
steps.trivial_justification: Fix arbitrary integers m >= 2 and g >= 0. Either g < m-1 or g >= m-1. In the first case, A5 gives N(m,g) <= N(m,g+1). In the second case, A4 gives N(m,g) <= N(m,g+1). Since one of these two cases always holds, the claimed inequality is true for all m >= 2 and g >= 0.

semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: If S is a numerical semigroup with multiplicity m, then {1,...,m-1} subseteq N0 \ S, hence g(S) >= m-1. Therefore A_{m,g} = emptyset and N(m,g)=0 for every g with 0 <= g < m-1.

lemmas.statement_nl: Let m be an integer with m >= 2. If S is a numerical semigroup with multiplicity m, then the integers 1,2,...,m-1 are not in S. Consequently g(S) >= m-1. Equivalently, for every integer g with 0 <= g < m-1, there exists no numerical semigroup S with multiplicity m and genus g, so A_{m,g} is empty and N(m,g)=0.

lemmas.statement_nl: Let m be an integer with m >= 2, and let S be a numerical semigroup with multiplicity m. Suppose g(S) >= m-1. Then S has at least one effective generator; that is, there exists x in S such that x is a minimal generator of S and x > F(S), where F(S) is the Frobenius number of S.

lemmas.statement_nl: Let m be an integer with m >= 2. Let S be a numerical semigroup with multiplicity m, and let x be an effective generator of S, meaning that x is a minimal generator of S and x > F(S). Define T = S \ {x}. Then T is a numerical semigroup, m(T)=m, g(T)=g(S)+1, and F(T)=x.

lemmas.statement_nl: Let m be an integer with m >= 2. Let T be a numerical semigroup with multiplicity m, and let y = F(T) be its Frobenius number. Define P = T ∪ {y}. Then P is a numerical semigroup, m(P)=m, g(P)=g(T)-1, and y is an effective generator of P.

semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: If T is obtained from S by deleting an effective generator x, then x = F(T) and therefore S = T union {F(T)}; hence the parent is uniquely determined by the child.

lemmas.statement_nl: Let m be an integer with m >= 2. Let S be a numerical semigroup with multiplicity m, let x be an effective generator of S, and define T = S \ {x}. Then S = T ∪ {F(T)}. Equivalently, the parent numerical semigroup S is uniquely recoverable from the child numerical semigroup T by adjoining the Frobenius number of T.

lemmas.statement_nl: Let m be an integer with m >= 2. For every numerical semigroup S with multiplicity m and genus g(S) >= m-1, define e(S) to be the least integer x such that x is an effective generator of S, and define C(S) = S \ {e(S)}. Then C(S) is well-defined, C(S) is a numerical semigroup with multiplicity m, and g(C(S)) = g(S)+1.

lemmas.statement_nl: Let m and g be integers with m >= 2 and g >= m-1. If there exists an injective function from A_{m,g} to A_{m,g+1}, where A_{m,h} denotes the set of numerical semigroups S with multiplicity m(S)=m and genus g(S)=h, then N(m,g) <= N(m,g+1), where N(m,h)=|A_{m,h}|.

shared_context.content: A numerical semigroup is a subset S of N0 = {0,1,2,...} such that 0 is in S, S is closed under addition, and N0 \ S is finite. The multiplicity m(S) is the least positive element of S. The genus g(S) is the cardinality of N0 \ S. If S is not equal to N0, its Frobenius number F(S) is the largest integer not in S. An element x in S \ {0} is a minimal generator of S if there do not exist a,b in S \ {0} with x = a + b. An effective generator of S is a minimal generator x satisfying x > F(S). For integers m >= 2 and g >= 0, let A_{m,g} = {S : S is a numerical semigroup, m(S)=m, g(S)=g}, and let N(m,g) = |A_{m,g}|.
shared_context.label: basic_definitions

candidates.strategy_summary: Use the numerical-semigroup tree at fixed multiplicity: for each numerical semigroup with multiplicity m, choose a canonical effective generator and delete it to obtain a child of the same multiplicity and genus increased by 1. Prove this child map is injective by recovering the parent uniquely from the Frobenius number of the child. Combine this with the fact that no numerical semigroup of multiplicity m has genus below m-1.
